english.title: Facilitate an unlicensed lottery - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) facilitated a lottery other than an exempt lottery by

(A)_[printing lottery tickets for a specified lottery]_
(B)_[printing promotional material for a specified lottery]_
(C)_[advertising a specified lottery]_

without acting in accordance with the terms and conditions of an operating licence
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 259(1) and 263(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
facilitated a lottery other than an exempt lottery by
printing lottery tickets for/printing promotional material for/advertising a specified lottery
without acting in accordance with the terms and conditions of an operating licence

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

english.notes:
(1) Section 259(4) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides defences to this offence.
(2) Section 259(5) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "promotional material" means a document which
(a) advertises a specified lottery,
(b) invites participation in a specified lottery,
(c) contains information about how to participate in a specified lottery, or
(d) lists winners in a specified lottery.
(3) For the territorial application of this offence see section 265 of the Gambling Act 2005. That section also includes a defence, where a person reasonably believed that the lottery was outside the territorial application of this offence.
(4) A licensing authority may institute criminal proceedings in respect of this offence, section 346(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
